Description: Susceptible individuals become infectious after being exposed to contaminated water.
Susceptible individuals are vaccinated and move directly to the recovered/immune compartment in a simple model.
Susceptible individuals receive a vaccine and move to a separate vaccinated compartment.
Infectious individuals recover from the disease and become immune.
Infectious individuals shed bacteria, contaminating the water supply.
Infected patients receive treatment, moving them to a treated compartment.
Immunity wanes over time, and recovered individuals become susceptible again.

Name: β
Description: Rate of 'contact' between the susceptible population with contaminated reservoir water.

Name: γ
Description: The per capita recovery rate from cholera infection.

Name: 1/δ
Description: The life span of cholera bacteria in the water reservoir.

Name: δ
Description: The removal or decay rate of V. cholerae bacteria from the water reservoir.

Name: ξ
Description: Rate of water contamination by humans, representing the rate of increase in V. cholerae concentration in the water reservoir.

Name: κ
Description: The concentration of cholera bacteria that yields a 50% chance of infection.

Name: R0
Description: The basic reproduction number, defined as the number of individuals that an infected individual can infect when introduced into a completely susceptible population.
